content: Linea nigra, derived from the Latin term meaning black line, is a dark vertical line that commonly appears on the abdomen during pregnancy. It is also referred to as linea nigra. This line is a manifestation of hyperpigmentation, which occurs due to an increased production of melanin. The process is believed to be driven by elevated estrogen levels, the same hormonal mechanism responsible for the darkening of the areolas during pregnancy. However, the specific reason why this hyperpigmentation occurs along the midline of the abdomen remains unclear. Women with lighter skin tones are less likely to exhibit this feature compared to those with darker skin pigmentation. Prior to its appearance, the line may be faintly visible as a linea alba, or white line. Linea nigra typically becomes noticeable around the second trimester of pregnancy. Some studies suggest a potential association between the development of linea nigra and insulin regulation. The characteristic appearance of linea nigra is a brownish streak, approximately one centimeter in width. It extends vertically along the midline of the abdomen, running from the pubic region to the xiphoid process, which is the lowermost part of the rib cage located at the tip of the sternum. No medical treatment is necessary for linea nigra. Dietary supplementation with folic acid has been suggested as a potential method to reduce the discoloration. After childbirth, the line gradually fades over time, although it may not completely disappear in some cases. Additionally, exposure to sunlight can cause the line to reappear.
